claims.text: What the strip looks like Widespread ST elevation in a usually benign pattern, common in young, healthy patients under 50.
claims.quote: Benign early repolarisation (BER) is a usually benign ECG pattern producing widespread ST segment elevation that is commonly seen in young, healthy patients < 50 years of age.

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) J point and ST: notched or slurred J point with concave ST elevation
claims.quote: Notched or slurred J point with concave ST elevation

claims.text: Where: most common in the precordial leads
ST elevation: widespread and concave, most prominent in the mid-to-left precordial leads (V2–5)
claims.quote: Widespread concave ST elevation, most prominent in the mid-to-left precordial leads (V2-5)

claims.text: J point notch: the “fish hook” pattern, often best seen in V4
claims.quote: One characteristic feature of BER is the presence of a notched or irregular J point: the so-called “fish hook” pattern. This is often best seen in lead V4.

claims.text: T waves: prominent, slightly asymmetrical, concordant with the QRS
claims.quote: Prominent, slightly asymmetrical T waves that are concordant with the QRS complex

claims.text: V6 ratio: ST elevation : T wave height < 0.25
claims.quote: ST elevation : T wave height ratio in V6 < 0.25

claims.text: Reciprocal changes: none suggesting occlusion MI
claims.quote: No reciprocal ST depression to suggest Occlusion MI

claims.text: Rate effect: the ST elevation may fluctuate with autonomic tone, diminishing with increased sympathetic tone, exercise or tachycardia and increasing as the heart rate slows
claims.quote: The degree of ST elevation may fluctuate in response to changes in autonomic tone, diminishing with increased sympathetic tone / exercise / tachycardia or increasing when the heart rate slows

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Usually in young, healthy patients
Mechanism: poorly understood; generally thought to be a normal variant, though the global BER pattern has recently been linked to future idiopathic VF
claims.quote: The physiological basis of BER is poorly understood. It is generally thought to be a normal variant that is not indicative of underlying cardiac disease, but recently a link has been made between the global BER pattern and future risk of idiopathic ventricular fibrillation (VF)

claims.text: Its widespread ST elevation may mimic pericarditis or acute MI
claims.quote: Widespread ST elevation in BER may mimic pericarditis or acute MI

claims.text: Up to 10–15% of ED chest-pain patients have BER on their ECG
claims.quote: Up to 10-15% of ED patients presenting with chest pain will have BER on their ECG

claims.text: Avoid diagnosing BER over age 50, especially with risk factors for ischemic heart disease
claims.quote: Avoid diagnosing BER in patients over the age of 50, especially those with risk factors for ischaemic heart disease.
